entries.grounds: mutant_view confirms `except (OSError, RangeError)` -> `except (RangeError,)` at adapters.py:338. The spawn-failure path is a RangeError, not an OSError: range_anchor.main() runs subprocess.Popen(req['argv']) in a SEPARATE anchor process (range_anchor.py:96-99) and on OSError reports 'SPAWN_FAILED {type}: {e}' over the pipe; the controller's ProcessRange.start() sees tag!='STARTED' and RAISES RangeError (process_range.py:363-365). So chmod-0644 (PermissionError) and the dead-interpreter case surface to _declared as RangeError, which (RangeError,) still catches -> unchanged. Residual OSError sources are _bounded's out.open('x') (adapters.py:347, inside _declared's try) and the controller's own Popen(sys.executable) (process_range.py:349) -- neither is a binary-identity failure and neither is reachable by any kill file (version.out is a fresh path in a fresh TemporaryDirectory; TMPDIR writable; sys.executable always launchable). MEASURED: test_v21_ocr_identity SURVIVED (OK 12.4s), which exercises both the chmod-0644 and #!/nonexistent/interpreter cases (test_v21_ocr_identity.py:204-218). Not provably EQUIVALENT (a hypothetical OSError in the try would propagate under the mutant vs. a clean (None,why) unmutated), but no consumer/contract/test/operator text depends on converting that I/O OSError to a refusal -> AUDITED.

entries.grounds: mutant_view confirms decode('utf-8','replace') -> decode('utf-8','') at adapters.py:340 (outside the except, so an error here is NOT caught). Verified the handler-lookup behaviour directly: valid UTF-8 -> '' returns the text (handler never consulted, == 'replace'); invalid bytes b'\xff\xfe' -> decode('utf-8','') raises LookupError: unknown error handler name '' (not OSError/RangeError, so it escapes _declared/_ocr/run.ocr_identity uncaught). The 'garbage' ANSWERS str (test_v21_ocr_declared.py:33) has \xff = U+00FF which encodes to VALID UTF-8 \xc3\xbf (raw \xff absent), so the fake binary's sys.stdout.write output is always valid UTF-8 and '' is never consulted -> no registered test reaches the crash. DIRECTLY DEMONSTRATED at the _declared level with a fake binary that does sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\xff\xfe not utf8\n'): UNMUTATED _declared returns (None, "...: `version` printed no version line (first line '\ufffd\ufffd not utf8')"); MUTANT raises LookupError: unknown error handler name ''. MEASURED: test_v21_ocr_identity SURVIVED (OK 13.4s). A real, unpinned robustness gap -> REFUTED (test owed).
entries.refutation: Reader: adapters._declared's decode feeding review_ocr.declared, and the gate contract that _declared returns (None, why) for ANY binary -- 'a refusal, never a traceback' (test_v21_ocr_identity.py:145; DECLARED_WAYS includes 'printed no version line':'no version line', :51-52; test_the_declared_operator_text_is_true_of_every_way_the_check_fails :186-202). Input: a binary whose `version` writes raw invalid UTF-8 bytes, e.g. sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\xff\xfe not utf8\n') -- NOT a Python str with U+00FF, which encodes to valid UTF-8. Sketch: in test_v21_ocr_identity.py (Identity, a registered kill file that drives the fake binary) extend FAKE_OCR's version branch (or add an ANSWERS entry consumed via sys.stdout.buffer.write) to emit raw bytes, then assert R.ocr_identity(self.settings())['status']=='REFUSED' and 'printed no version line' in reason and no exception is raised. Equivalent direct unit test (reproduced here, PASSES unmutated / raises under the mutant): point the exe at a binary printing b'\xff\xfe' and assert adapters._declared(exe, review_ocr.VERSION_TIMEOUT_S) == (None, <why containing 'printed no version line'>), not a raised LookupError.
